item.text:
{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"Treat d1o5dt2 as an incomplete family member, not as evidence for a naturally reduced fibronectin type III architecture. In SCOPe 2.08, d1o5dt2 (SUNID 103884; 1o5d T:107–205) has the domain-specific annotation “fr”: missing more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence. d1uc6a1 (SUNID 107766; 1uc6 A:6–109) has no corresponding fragment flag; absence of that flag alone does not establish coordinate completeness or quality.

For alignment, compare the homologous sequence and structural core actually present, explicitly marking unavailable regions. Do not score missing coordinates as evolutionary deletions or force a whole-domain structural alignment. Report aligned residue count and coverage alongside identity or structural similarity: a good match over a small retained region can conceal substantial incompleteness. Establish exactly what is missing by checking deposited sequence, observed coordinates, domain boundaries, and construct information; nominal residue spans alone are insufficient.

For a general family representative or whole-domain template, provisionally prefer d1uc6a1, subject to checks of completeness, experimental quality, and relevance to the target. Retain d1o5dt2 as a clearly labeled fragment when its tissue-factor context or retained region is useful, but do not use it alone to infer missing strands, loops, interfaces, or full-domain geometry.

Both belong to family b.1.2.1 and superfamily b.1.2, supporting common ancestry. Their fold b.1 is the immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich, and class b is all-beta proteins; fold or class membership alone does not establish homology. d1uc6a1 comes from ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, whereas d1o5dt2 comes from the extracellular region of human tissue factor. These illustrate different protein contexts within the family, but the fragment's apparent structural losses must not inflate estimates of evolutionary diversity. Family membership does not justify transferring their receptor, ligand-binding, or coagulation functions; such transfer requires independent functional and binding-site evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/annotations"]}]}
